evidence.quote: One potential threat arises from the choice of backbone models used in our evaluation. Due to budget constraints, we primarily evaluate on five open-source or open-weight models.
One potential threat concerns whether the evaluation metrics used in our study are sufficient to fully capture the quality of automated issue resolution.
In particular, the assessment of the quality of reproduction tests and edge tests relies on the judgment of an analysis agent, which may introduce a subjective bias.

PhoenixRepair incurs an average cost of $0.154 per task, compared to $0.083 for SWE-agent, $0.079 for Mini-SWE-agent, and $0.080 for Live-SWE-agent. This corresponds to approximately a 1.85× overhead over the SWE-agent.
